excerpt_i18n.en: Meta's multi-billion dollar acquisition of Manus reflects its confidence in the evolution of "intelligent capability" from "brain-only" to "brain-and-hand" proficiency. IT veteran Li Guoping commented on Manus's change of ownership, noting that the "intelligent capability" refers to the composite ability of intelligent agents (Agents) in both cognition and execution. In his view, the SaaS industry is also undergoing its own intelligent transformation—"If SaaS continues to rely primarily on human-system (interface) interaction without embracing intelligent transformation, it will inevitably be overturned by the times." The fundamental shift in human-computer interaction models represents a disruptive change brought by the Agent wave to the SaaS industry. This assertion stems from Li Guoping's decades of firsthand experience with transformative turning points: during the software era, operating systems were the core of the digital world; in the PC internet era, portals and later search engines became the gateways to the digital world, which shifted to apps in the mobile internet era; and in the cloud computing era, SaaS integrated and encapsulated all capabilities. Li Guoping, who worked at Microsoft for over a decade, currently serves as the Dean of the Digital Economy and Fintech Research Institute at Baiwang Co., Ltd., a leading domestic tax and finance SaaS provider. Over the nearly 20 years since the rise of cloud computing, he has consistently embraced and adopted new technological waves. Where will the future of SaaS head under the Agent wave? In Li Guoping's view, SaaS is unlikely to disappear within the next five years but will first transition toward embedded, localized intelligent applications.

Spirit, the soul, is what robots urgently need today. Yet over the past year, the souls of robots have oscillated between two extremes. On one end, dazzling videos repeatedly flood screens, with highly structured experimental "greenhouses" continuously producing high-success-rate models, making AI in demos appear incredibly intelligent. On the other end, when these "top performers" enter the real world, they frequently stumble. Demo videos can be edited, lab environments can be customized, and task difficulty can be tailored. This has plunged the entire industry into a "Guan Gong vs. Qin Qiong" dilemma: with varying scenarios, hardware, and evaluation standards, what exactly are we comparing? Is it technology, intelligence, or whose cinematography and editing are more professional?

This unfocused competition welcomed its first "chief referee" by the end of 2025. In the first month of 2026, this "chief referee" crowned the first Chinese champion. The top spot, long dominated by Pi0.5, changed hands. On January 12, Qianxun Intelligence open-sourced its self-developed VLA model Spirit v1.5, which soared to the top of the Table30 leaderboard by RoboChallenge—a third-party robot model evaluation organization jointly initiated by Dexmal and Hugging Face—surpassing the previous strongest model, Pi0.5.

Por un lado, diversos videos deslumbrantes han inundado repetidamente las pantallas, y los "invernaderos" experimentales altamente estructurados han producido continuamente modelos con altas tasas de éxito; en los demos, la IA parece tan inteligente.
